To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bottom-up development is more evolvable than top-down development.
bottom-up orientation during development increases the evolvability of the resulting software system.
software evolution is a bottom-up process and that the construction of evolvability is a top-down process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two questions: How can we proceed bottom-up in software development to achieve evolvable artefacts? How can we improve the evolvability of bottom-up developed systems?
the question how the construction of software should be changed in order to improve the evolvability of software systems.
the development of new development processes which support the construction of evolvability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a bottom-up approach is superior to top-down for evolvability, but that top-down has to be used in the beginning.
bottom-up development is the better choice for evolvable software.
bottom-up development is superior to top-down development with respect to the evolvability of the resulting software systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bottom-up is good, top-down is evil, and that we need new development processes to support bottom-up development.
bottom-up orientation should be the default strategy during software evolution.
the decision to develop software bottom-up or top-down should not be taken by the developer but rather by the software itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bottom-up development is a promising way to improve software evolvability, and that the current development processes are not well suited for it.
bottom-up orientation is not a silver bullet for software evolution.
bottom-up development is the key to future evolvability and that the development process should reflect this.
